top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice clock is a distinct mechanism from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes: it cancels the trap light shift while holding thousands of neutral atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, giving accuracy and averaging power together at about 1e-18. It has been reproduced independently at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and NPL, so it is mature without waiting for the SI redefinition, and the credit to Katori (proposal and first realization) and Ye (record accuracy and many-body control) is clean. Awarding it with a narrow citation is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; he works in a neighbouring AMO and precision-measurement area but has no stated connection to Katori or Ye
